title.zh: 卷二百一十八 列傳第一百四十三 沙陀
title.raw: 卷二百一十八 列傳第一百四十三 沙陀 Volume 218 Biographies 143: Shatuo

sentences.zh: 沙陀，西突厥別部處月種也。

translations.literal: The Shatuo were of the Chuyue branch among the dependent tribes of the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo were a branch of the Chuyue people, a dependent tribe of the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 始，突厥東西部分治烏孫故地，與處月、處蜜雜居。

translations.literal: At first, when the Eastern and Western Turks divided rule over the former Wusun lands, they lived intermixed with the Chuyue and Chumi.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, as the Eastern and Western Turks partitioned the old Wusun territories, they dwelt alongside the Chuyue and Chumi peoples.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，太宗以鼓纛立利邲咄陸可汗，而族人步真觖望，謀並其弟彌射乃自立。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, Taizong installed Ashina Yipiduolu as khan with the drum-and-banner ceremony; the clansman Böke was discontented and plotted to join his younger brother Mishe and declare himself ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 (633), Emperor Taizong invested Ashina Yipiduolu as khan in the formal drum-and-banner ceremony. A clansman named Böke, resentful of the appointment, conspired to ally with his younger brother Mishe and seize power for himself.

sentences.zh: 彌射懼，率處月等入朝。

translations.literal: Mishe was afraid and led the Chuyue and others to submit to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his safety, Mishe led the Chuyue and other tribes to present themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 而步真勢窮，亦歸國。

translations.literal: Böke, his strength exhausted, also returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Böke, his position hopeless, likewise submitted to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 其留者，咄陸以射匱特勒劫越之子賀魯統之。

translations.literal: Those who remained were placed under Helu, son of the Shegui tegin Jeučü, by Ashina Duolu.
translations.idiomatic: Those who stayed behind were placed under Helu, son of the Shegui tegin Jeučü, by Ashina Duolu.

sentences.zh: 西突厥浸強，內相攻，其大酋乙毗咄陸可汗建廷鏃曷山之西，號北庭，而處月等又隸屬之。

translations.literal: The Western Turks grew stronger and fought among themselves; their great chief Ashina Yipiduolu established his court west of Mount Zhuo'e, calling it Beiting, and the Chuyue and others again came under his rule.
translations.idiomatic: As the Western Turks grew more powerful and turned on one another, their paramount leader Ashina Yipiduolu set up his court west of Mount Zhuo'e and styled it Beiting; the Chuyue and related peoples once again fell under his authority.

sentences.zh: 處月居金娑山之陽，蒲類之東，有大磧，名沙陀，故號沙陀突厥雲。

translations.literal: The Chuyue dwelt south of Mount Jinsuo and east of Pulei; there was a great desert called Shatuo, hence they were called the Shatuo Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The Chuyue lived south of Mount Jinsuo and east of Pulei, in a vast desert known as Shatuo—whence they came to be called the Shatuo Turks.

sentences.zh: 咄陸寇伊州，引二部兵圍天山，安西都護郭孝恪擊走之，拔處月俟斤之城。

translations.literal: Duolu raided Yizhou, leading troops of both tribes to besiege Tianshan; Protector-General of Anxi Guo Xiaoke routed him and took the Chuyue yabghu's city.
translations.idiomatic: Duolu attacked Yizhou and led warriors from both tribes to encircle Tianshan. Guo Xiaoke, Protector-General of Anxi, drove him off and captured the Chuyue yabghu's stronghold.

sentences.zh: 後乙毗可汗敗，奔吐火羅。

translations.literal: Later the Yipiduolu khan was defeated and fled to Tuhuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ashina Yipiduolu was defeated and fled to Tokharistan.

sentences.zh: 賀魯來降，詔拜瑤池都督，徙其部庭州之莫賀城。

translations.literal: Helu came to surrender; an edict appointed him Protector of Yaochi and moved his tribe to Mohe City in Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Helu submitted to the Tang. The court appointed him Protector of Yaochi and resettled his people at Mohe City in Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 處月朱邪闕俟斤阿厥亦請內屬。

translations.literal: The Chuyue Zhuye yabghu Aque also requested to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Chuyue Zhuye yabghu Aque likewise petitioned to come under Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，賀魯反，而朱邪孤註亦殺招慰使連和，引兵據牢山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, Helu rebelled; Zhuye Guzhu also killed the pacification commissioner Lianhe and led troops to hold Laoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui era, Helu rose in revolt. Zhuye Guzhu killed the pacification commissioner Lianhe and seized Laoshan with his forces.

sentences.zh: 於是射脾俟斤沙陀那速不肯從，高宗以賀魯所領授之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Shepi yabghu Shatuo Nasu refused to follow Helu; Gaozong granted him the followers Helu had led.
translations.idiomatic: The Shepi yabghu Shatuo Nasu refused to join the rebellion, and Emperor Gaozong transferred to him the followers who had been under Helu's command.

sentences.zh: 明年，弓月道總管梁建方、契何力引兵斬孤註，俘九千人。

translations.literal: The next year, Gongyue Circuit Commander Liang Jianfang and Qibi Heli led troops to behead Guzhu and took nine thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Liang Jianfang, commander of the Gongyue circuit, and Qibi Heli marched against Guzhu, killed him, and took nine thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 又明年，廢瑤池都督府，即處月地置金滿、沙陀二州，皆領都督。

translations.literal: The year after that, the Yaochi Protectorate was abolished; on Chuyue territory Jinman and Shatuo prefectures were established, each with a commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the year after that the Yaochi Protectorate was abolished, and on Chuyue lands the court set up the Jinman and Shatuo prefectures, each headed by a commander.

sentences.zh: 賀魯亡，安撫大使阿史那彌射次伊麗水，而處月來歸。

translations.literal: When Helu perished, Pacification Commissioner Ashina Mishe encamped on the Ili River, and the Chuyue returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Helu's defeat, Pacification Commissioner Ashina Mishe took position on the Ili River, and the Chuyue submitted once more.

sentences.zh: 乃置昆陵都護府，統咄陸部，以彌射為都護。

translations.literal: The Kunling Protectorate was then established to govern the Duolu tribes, with Mishe as protector.
translations.idiomatic: The court then established the Kunling Protectorate to govern the Duolu tribes, appointing Mishe as protector.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，以處月酋沙陀金山從武衛將軍薛仁貴討鐵勒，授墨離軍討擊使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longshuo, the Chuyue chief Shatuo Jinshan followed Martial Guard General Xue Rengui against the Tiele and was made Mohe Army strike commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longshuo era the Chuyue chief Shatuo Jinshan accompanied Martial Guard General Xue Rengui in the campaign against the Tiele and was appointed strike commander of the Mohe Army.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，進為金滿州都督，累封張掖郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an he was promoted to commander of Jinman Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 2 (702) he was promoted to commander of Jinman Prefecture and eventually enfeoffed as Duke of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 金山死，子輔國嗣。

translations.literal: Jinshan died; his son Fuguo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinshan died, his son Fuguo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 先天初避吐蕃，徙部北庭，率其下入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantian, fleeing the Tibetans, he moved his tribe to Beiting and led his people to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiantian era, fleeing Tibetan pressure, he relocated his tribe to Beiting and led his followers to present themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，復領金滿州都督，封其母鼠尼施為鄯國夫人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan he again held command of Jinman Prefecture; his mother Shunishi was ennobled as Lady of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 2 (714) he was again appointed commander of Jinman Prefecture, and his mother Shunishi was ennobled as Lady of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 輔國累爵永壽郡王。

translations.literal: Fuguo was repeatedly ennobled as Prince of Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo was eventually enfeoffed as Prince of Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 死，子骨咄支嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Gutuzhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death his son Gutuzhi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，回紇內附，以骨咄支兼回紇副都護。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, when the Uyghurs submitted, Gutuzhi was made deputy protector of the Uyghurs as well.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era, when the Uyghurs came under Tang rule, Gutuzhi was also appointed deputy protector over them.

sentences.zh: 從肅宗平安祿山，拜特進、驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Suzong in pacifying An Lushan and was appointed Special Advancement and General of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Suzong in suppressing An Lushan and was appointed Special Advancement and general of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 死，子盡忠嗣，累遷金吾衛大將軍、酒泉縣公。

translations.literal: He died; his son Jinzhong succeeded and was promoted to Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard and Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his son Jinzhong succeeded him and rose to Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard and Duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 至德、寶應間，中國多故，北庭、西州閉不通，朝奏使皆道出回紇，而虜多漁擷，尤苦之，雖沙陀之倚北庭者，亦困其暴斂。

translations.literal: Between Zhide and Baoying, China was in turmoil; Beiting and Xizhou were cut off; court envoys all went by way of the Uyghurs, who plundered heavily—the Shatuo who relied on Beiting also suffered from their exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Zhide and Baoying eras China was torn by upheaval. Beiting and Xizhou were sealed off, and all envoys to court had to travel through Uyghur lands, where they were preyed upon relentlessly. Even the Shatuo, who still looked to Beiting, were ground down by Uyghur exactions.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，沙陀部七千帳附吐蕃，與共寇北庭，陷之。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan, seven thousand Shatuo households submitted to the Tibetans, joined them in attacking Beiting, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era seven thousand Shatuo households submitted to Tibet and joined in the assault on Beiting, which fell to the combined forces.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃徙其部甘州，以盡忠為軍大論。

translations.literal: The Tibetans moved the tribe to Ganzhou and made Jinzhong army chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet resettled the tribe in Ganzhou and appointed Jinzhong army chief minister.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇邊，常以沙陀為前鋒。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans raided the borders, they regularly used the Shatuo as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tibet raided the frontier, the Shatuo were regularly sent as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 久之，回鶻取涼州，吐蕃疑盡忠持兩端，議徙沙陀於河外，舉部愁恐。

translations.literal: After a time the Uyghurs took Liangzhou; the Tibetans suspected Jinzhong of double-dealing and proposed moving the Shatuo beyond the river—the whole tribe was filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: In time the Uyghurs seized Liangzhou. Tibet, suspecting Jinzhong of playing both sides, proposed relocating the Shatuo beyond the Yellow River, and the entire tribe was seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 盡忠與朱邪執宜謀，曰：「我世為唐臣，不幸陷汙，今若走蕭關自歸，不愈於絕種乎？」

translations.literal: Jinzhong plotted with Zhuye Zhuyi, saying, "We have been Tang subjects for generations; having fallen into defilement, if we now flee through Xiaoguan to return on our own, is that not better than extinction?
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong took counsel with Zhuye Zhuyi. "We have been subjects of the Tang for generations," he said. "Though we have fallen into shameful servitude, if we break for Xiaoguan and return to the dynasty of our own accord, is that not better than being wiped out?

sentences.zh: 盡忠曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Jinzhong said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong replied, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 元和三年，悉眾三萬落循烏德山而東。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe, with all their people—thirty thousand households—they followed Mount Wude eastward.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 3 (808) the whole tribe—thirty thousand households—set out eastward along Mount Wude.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃追之。

translations.literal: The Tibetans pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan forces gave chase.

sentences.zh: 行且戰，旁洮水，奏石門，轉鬥不解，部眾略盡，盡忠死之。

translations.literal: Marching and fighting, they went along the Tao River, passed Shimen, and fought without respite until the tribe was nearly gone and Jinzhong died.
translations.idiomatic: They marched and fought along the Tao River, passed through Shimen, and battled without respite until the tribe was nearly destroyed and Jinzhong fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 執宜裒瘢傷，士裁二千，騎七百，雜畜橐它千計，款靈州塞。

translations.literal: Zhuyi gathered the wounded; soldiers numbered only two thousand, horsemen seven hundred, and mixed livestock and camels about a thousand; he presented himself at the Lingzhou frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyi gathered the wounded survivors—barely two thousand foot soldiers and seven hundred horsemen, with roughly a thousand head of livestock and camels—and presented himself at the Lingzhou frontier.

sentences.zh: 節度使範希朝以聞。

translations.literal: Military Governor Fan Xichao reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor Fan Xichao reported the arrival to court.

sentences.zh: 詔處其部鹽州，置陰山府，以執宜為府兵馬使。

translations.literal: An edict settled the tribe in Yanzhou, established the Yinshan Garrison, and made Zhuyi garrison horse commander.
translations.idiomatic: An edict resettled the tribe in Yanzhou, established the Yinshan Garrison, and appointed Zhuyi its horse commander.

sentences.zh: 沙陀素健鬥，希朝欲藉以捍虜，為市牛羊，廣畜牧，休養之。

translations.literal: The Shatuo were naturally fierce in battle; Xichao wished to use them against the barbarians, bought cattle and sheep for them, expanded their herding, and let them rest.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo were renowned fighters. Xichao meant to use them against the frontier enemies, bought cattle and sheep on their behalf, expanded their herds, and gave them time to recover.

sentences.zh: 其童耄自鳳翔、興元、太原道歸者，皆還其部。

translations.literal: Children and elders returning from Fengxiang, Xingyuan, and Taiyuan were all sent back to the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Children and elders who had strayed to Fengxiang, Xingyuan, and Taiyuan were all returned to the tribe.

sentences.zh: 盡忠弟葛勒阿波率殘部七百叩振武降，授左武衛大將軍，兼陰山府都督。

translations.literal: Jinzhong's younger brother Geleabo led seven hundred survivors to knock at Zhenwu and surrender; he was made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and concurrently commander of the Yinshan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong's younger brother Geleabo led seven hundred survivors to Zhenwu to surrender. He was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and concurrently commander of the Yinshan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 執宜朝長安，賜金幣袍馬萬計，授特進、金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Zhuyi attended court at Chang'an; he was given gold, coins, robes, and horses in the tens of thousands, and appointed Special Advancement and General of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyi came to court at Chang'an and received lavish gifts of gold, coin, robes, and horses numbering in the tens of thousands. He was appointed Special Advancement and general of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 然議者以靈武迫吐蕃，恐後反覆生變，又濱邊，益口則食翔價。

translations.literal: Yet critics said Lingwu was close to Tibet and feared later reversals; moreover it bordered the frontier—more mouths would raise grain prices.
translations.idiomatic: Critics objected that Lingwu lay too close to Tibet and might invite future trouble, and that settling more people on the frontier would drive up grain prices.

sentences.zh: 頃之，希朝鎮太原，因詔沙陀舉軍從之。

translations.literal: Before long Xichao took command at Taiyuan; an edict then ordered the Shatuo to bring their army and follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xichao was posted to Taiyuan, and an edict ordered the Shatuo to march their forces under his command.

sentences.zh: 希朝乃料其勁騎千二百，號沙陀軍，置軍使，而處餘眾於定襄川。

translations.literal: Xichao then selected twelve hundred of their best horsemen, called them the Shatuo Army, appointed an army commander, and settled the rest at Dingxiang River.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao selected twelve hundred of their finest horsemen, organized them as the Shatuo Army under a dedicated commander, and resettled the remainder along the Dingxiang River.

sentences.zh: 執宜乃保神武川之黃花堆，更號陰山北沙陀。

translations.literal: Zhuyi then held Huanghuadui on the Shenwu River and was again called the Northern Shatuo of Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyi established himself at Huanghuadui on the Shenwu River and took the name Northern Shatuo of Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 是時，天子伐鎮州，執宜以軍七百為前鋒，王承宗眾數萬伏木刀溝，與執宜遇，飛矢雨集。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven attacked Zhenzhou; Zhuyi led seven hundred men as vanguard. Wang Chengzong's tens of thousands lay in ambush at Mudao Ravine; they met Zhuyi and arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then campaigning against Zhenzhou. Zhuyi led seven hundred men as the vanguard. Wang Chengzong had tens of thousands lying in wait at Mudao Ravine; when they met Zhuyi's force, arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 執宜提軍橫貫賊陣鏖鬥，李光顏等乘之，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: Zhuyi led his army straight through the rebel lines in fierce combat; Li Guangyan and others pressed the advantage and took ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyi drove his troops straight through the rebel formation in savage fighting. Li Guangyan and the other Tang commanders pressed the advantage and claimed ten thousand enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵解，進蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: The Zhenzhou army was relieved; he was promoted to prefect of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With the siege of Zhenzhou lifted, he was promoted to prefect of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 王鍔節度太原，建言：「朱邪族孳熾，散居北川，恐啟野心，願析其族隸諸州，勢分易弱也。」

translations.literal: Wang E, military governor of Taiyuan, memorialized: "The Zhuye clan is multiplying and scattered in the northern valleys; I fear they may harbor ambition. I wish to divide the clan among the prefectures so their strength is split and they are easily weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, military governor of Taiyuan, memorialized: "The Zhuye clan is growing rapidly and scattered through the northern valleys. I fear they may turn ambitious. I propose dividing them among the prefectures so their strength is dispersed and they are easier to control.

sentences.zh: 遂建十府以處沙陀。

translations.literal: Ten garrisons were then established to settle the Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: The court accordingly established ten garrisons to resettle the Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 八年，回鶻過磧南取西城、柳谷，詔執宜屯天德。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Uyghurs crossed south of the desert and took Xicheng and Liugu; Zhuyi was ordered to garrison Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Uyghurs crossed south of the desert and seized Xicheng and Liugu. Zhuyi was ordered to garrison Tiande.

sentences.zh: 明年，伐吳元濟，又詔執宜隸李光顏，破蔡人時曲，拔淩雲柵。

translations.literal: The next year, campaigning against Wu Yuanji, Zhuyi was again ordered under Li Guangyan; he broke the Cai forces at Shiqu and took Lingyun Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the campaign against Wu Yuanji, Zhuyi was again placed under Li Guangyan. He routed the Cai forces at Shiqu and captured Lingyun Stockade.

sentences.zh: 元濟平，授檢校刑部尚書，猶隸光顏軍。

translations.literal: When Yuanji was pacified, he was made Acting Minister of Justice but still served under Guangyan's army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanji's defeat he was appointed Acting Minister of Justice while remaining under Li Guangyan's command.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，伐鎮州，悉發沙陀，與易定軍掎角，破賊深州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, attacking Zhenzhou, all Shatuo were mobilized; with the Yiding army in pincer they broke the rebels at Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era, in the campaign against Zhenzhou, every Shatuo fighter was mobilized. Working in concert with the Yiding army, they routed the rebels at Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 執宜入朝，留宿衛，拜金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Zhuyi came to court, remained in palace guard service, and was appointed General of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyi came to court, was retained in the palace guard, and appointed general of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 大和中，柳公綽領河東，奏陘北沙陀素為九姓、六州所畏，請委執宜治雲、朔塞下廢府十一，料部人三千禦北邊，號代北行營，授執宜陰山府都督、代北行營招撫使，隸河東節度。

translations.literal: In Dahe, Liu Gongchuo commanded Hedong and memorialized that the northern Shatuo were long feared by the Nine Surnames and Six Prefectures; he asked to entrust Zhuyi with eleven abandoned garrisons below Yun and Shuo, muster three thousand tribesmen to guard the north, call it the Northern Dai Camp, and appoint Zhuyi commander of Yinshan Garrison and pacification commissioner of the Northern Dai Camp under Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dahe era Liu Gongchuo took command of Hedong and memorialized that the Shatuo of the northern passes had long been feared by the Nine Surnames and the Six Prefectures. He proposed putting Zhuyi in charge of eleven abandoned garrisons below Yun and Shuo, mustering three thousand tribesmen to guard the northern frontier under the title Northern Dai Camp, and appointing Zhuyi commander of the Yinshan Garrison and pacification commissioner of that camp under Hedong command.

sentences.zh: 執宜死，子赤心嗣。

translations.literal: Zhuyi died; his son Chixin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuyi died, his son Chixin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 開成四年，回鶻徑磧口，抵榆林塞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng the Uyghurs went straight through the desert pass and reached Yulin frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 4 (839) the Uyghurs marched straight through the desert pass and reached the Yulin frontier.

sentences.zh: 宰相掘羅勿以良馬三百遺赤心，約共攻彰信可汗。

translations.literal: Chancellor Jueluowu sent Chixin three hundred fine horses and agreed to attack Khan Zhangxin together.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Jueluowu sent Chixin three hundred fine horses and proposed a joint attack on Khan Zhangxin.

sentences.zh: 可汗死，節度使劉沔以沙陀擊回鶻於殺胡山。

translations.literal: When the khan died, Military Governor Liu Mian used the Shatuo to strike the Uyghurs at Shahu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After the khan's death, Military Governor Liu Mian led the Shatuo against the Uyghurs at Shahu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 久之，伐潞，誅劉稹，詔赤心率代北騎軍三千隸石雄為前軍，破石會關，助王宰下天井，合太原軍，次榆社，與監軍使呂義忠禽楊弁。

translations.literal: After a time, campaigning against Lu to execute Liu Zhen, Chixin was ordered to lead three thousand Northern Dai cavalry under Shi Xiong as vanguard; they broke Shihui Pass, helped Wang Zai take Tianjing, joined the Taiyuan army, encamped at Yushe, and with Army Supervisor Lü Yizhong captured Yang Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the campaign against Lu to execute Liu Zhen, Chixin was ordered to lead three thousand Northern Dai horsemen under Shi Xiong as the vanguard. They stormed Shihui Pass, helped Wang Zai take Tianjing, joined forces with the Taiyuan army, encamped at Yushe, and together with Army Supervisor Lü Yizhong captured Yang Bian.

sentences.zh: 潞州平，遷朔州刺史，仍為代北軍使。

translations.literal: When Luzhou was pacified, he was moved to prefect of Shuozhou and remained Northern Dai army commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Luzhou was pacified he was transferred to prefect of Shuozhou while retaining command of the Northern Dai army.

sentences.zh: 大中初，吐蕃合党項及回鶻殘眾寇河西，太原王宰統代北諸軍進討，沙陀常深入，冠諸軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong, Tibet joined the Tangut and Uyghur remnants to raid Hexi; Wang Zai of Taiyuan led the Northern Dai armies forward—the Shatuo often penetrated deepest and led all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong era Tibet allied with Tangut and remnant Uyghur forces to raid Hexi. Wang Zai of Taiyuan led the Northern Dai armies in the counteroffensive; the Shatuo habitually pushed deepest and outfought every other contingent.

sentences.zh: 赤心所向，虜輒披靡，曰：「吾見赤馬將軍火生頭上。」

translations.literal: Wherever Chixin advanced, the enemy broke; they said, "I see the red-horse general with fire atop his head.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Chixin led, the enemy broke and fled. "I see the Red-Horse General with fire blazing above his head," they would say.

sentences.zh: 始，沙陀臣吐蕃，其左老右壯，混男女，略與同，而馳射趫悍過之，虜倚其兵，常苦邊。

translations.literal: At first, when the Shatuo served Tibet, elders on the left and warriors on the right, men and women mingled much like the Tibetans, yet in mounted archery they were swifter and fiercer; the barbarians relied on their troops and constantly harried the borders.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shatuo first served Tibet, their formation placed elders on the left and warriors on the right, with men and women intermingled much like Tibetan custom; yet in mounted archery they were swifter and fiercer still. Tibet leaned on their strength and they constantly ravaged the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及歸國，吐蕃由此亦衰。

translations.literal: When they returned to the Tang, Tibet thereby also declined.
translations.idiomatic: Once they returned to Tang allegiance, Tibetan power waned accordingly.

sentences.zh: 宣宗已復三州、七關，征西戍皆罷，乃遷赤心蔚州刺史、雲州守捉使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had already recovered the Three Prefectures and Seven Passes; western garrisons were all withdrawn, and Chixin was moved to prefect of Youzhou and Yunzhou frontier commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanzong had recovered the Three Prefectures and Seven Passes and withdrawn the western expeditionary forces, Chixin was appointed prefect of Youzhou and frontier commander of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 龐勛亂，詔義成康承訓為行營招討使，赤心以突騎三千從。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun rebelled, Kang Chengxun of Yicheng was made campaign pacification commissioner; Chixin followed with three thousand shock cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun rose in rebellion, Kang Chengxun of Yicheng was appointed campaign pacification commissioner, and Chixin followed with three thousand shock cavalry.

sentences.zh: 承訓兵絕渙水，遇伏，墮圍中幾沒，赤心以騎五百掀出之。

translations.literal: Chengxun's army was cut off at the Huan River, met an ambush, and nearly perished in encirclement; Chixin with five hundred horsemen burst in and pulled them out.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun's army was cut off at the Huan River, ambushed, and nearly destroyed. Chixin charged in with five hundred horsemen and wrenched them free.

sentences.zh: 勛欲速戰，眾八萬，短兵接，赤心勒勁騎突賊，與官軍夾擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Xun wished a quick battle; his force was eighty thousand; in close combat Chixin drove elite cavalry into the rebels and, with government troops on both sides, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sought a decisive battle with eighty thousand men. In close fighting Chixin drove his elite cavalry into the rebel ranks while government forces struck from both flanks, and the rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 其弟赤衰以千騎追之亳東。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chishuai pursued east of Bo with a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chishuai pursued with a thousand horsemen east of Bo.

sentences.zh: 勛平，進大同軍節度使，賜氏李，名國昌，預鄭王屬籍，賜親仁裏甲第。

translations.literal: When Xun was pacified, he was promoted to military governor of Datong Army; the surname Li was granted, name Guochang; he was entered in Prince Zheng's clan register and given a mansion in Qinren Lane.
translations.idiomatic: After Pang Xun's defeat he was promoted to military governor of the Datong Army, granted the surname Li and the name Guochang, enrolled in Prince Zheng's clan register, and given a mansion in Qinren Lane.

sentences.zh: 回鶻叩榆林，擾靈、鹽，詔國昌為鄜延節度使。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs knocked at Yulin and harassed Ling and Yan; Guochang was ordered as military governor of Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs pressed Yulin and raided Ling and Yan, Guochang was appointed military governor of Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 又寇天德，乃徙節振武，進檢校司徒。

translations.literal: They again raided Tiande; he was then moved to command Zhenwu and promoted to Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When they raided Tiande again, his command was shifted to Zhenwu and he was promoted to Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 王仙芝陷荊、襄，朝廷發諸州兵討捕，國昌遣劉遷統雲中突騎逐賊，數有功。

translations.literal: Wang Xianzhi took Jing and Xiang; the court mobilized troops from all prefectures; Guochang sent Liu Qian leading Yunzhong shock cavalry to pursue the bandits with repeated success.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xianzhi seized Jing and Xiang, the court mobilized troops from every prefecture. Guochang sent Liu Qian at the head of Yunzhong shock cavalry to hunt the rebels, with repeated success.

sentences.zh: 乾符三年，段文楚為代北水陸發運、雲州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianfu, Duan Wenchu was made Northern Dai land-and-water transport commissioner and Yunzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu 3 (876) Duan Wenchu was appointed Northern Dai land-and-water transport commissioner and defense commissioner of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時無年，文楚晙損用度，下皆怨。

translations.literal: There were bad harvests; Wenchu sharply cut expenditures and all below resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests had failed and Wenchu sharply cut expenditures; his subordinates were bitterly resentful.

sentences.zh: 邊校程懷信、王行審、蓋寓、李存璋、薛鐵山、康君立等曹議曰：「世多難，丈夫當投罅立功。

translations.literal: Frontier officers Cheng Huaixin, Wang Xingshen, Gai Yu, Li Cunzhang, Xue Tieshan, Kang Junli and others plotted together, saying, "The age is full of troubles; a man should thrust into a gap and win merit.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officers Cheng Huaixin, Wang Xingshen, Gai Yu, Li Cunzhang, Xue Tieshan, Kang Junli, and others plotted together. "These are troubled times," they said. "A man should seize his chance and win glory.

sentences.zh: 段公乃儒者，難共計。

translations.literal: Lord Duan is a Confucian scholar—hard to plan with.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Duan is a bookish scholar—we cannot plan with him.

sentences.zh: 沙陀雄勁，李振武父子勇冠軍，我若推之，無不應，則代北唾手可定。

translations.literal: The Shatuo are fierce; Li Zhenwu and his son are boldest in the army. If we raise them, none will refuse; then Northern Dai is ours in a snap.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo are formidable, and Li Zhenwu and his son are the boldest fighters in the army. If we put them forward, everyone will follow, and Northern Dai will be ours in an instant.

sentences.zh: 拾取富貴若何？」

translations.literal: What of scooping up wealth and rank?
translations.idiomatic: Why not seize wealth and rank for ourselves?

sentences.zh: 咸曰：「善！」

translations.literal: All said, "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: All agreed: "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 乃夜謁國昌子雲中守捉使克用曰：「歲艱稟食削，吾等不忍餓死，公家威德著聞，請誅虐帥，安部內。」

translations.literal: That night they visited Guochang's son, Yunzhou frontier commander Keyong, saying, "Years are hard and rations cut—we cannot bear to starve. Your house's prestige is renowned; please kill the cruel commander and settle the tribe."
translations.idiomatic: That night they visited Guochang's son Keyong, frontier commander of Yunzhou. "Hard times have cut our rations," they said, "and we will not starve in silence. Your family's renown is great—kill the cruel commander and bring peace to the tribe."

sentences.zh: 克用許之，募得士萬人，趨雲州，次鬥雞臺。

translations.literal: Keyong agreed, mustered ten thousand men, hurried to Yunzhou, and encamped at Douji Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong agreed, raised ten thousand men, marched on Yunzhou, and encamped at Douji Terrace.

sentences.zh: 城中執文楚至，殺之；

translations.literal: The city seized Wenchu and brought him forth; he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The city seized Wenchu and brought him out; he was killed.

sentences.zh: 據州以聞，共丐克用為大同防禦留後。

translations.literal: They held the prefecture and reported it; all begged Keyong as acting Datong defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They held the prefecture and reported to court, jointly petitioning for Keyong as acting Datong defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 不許，發諸道兵進捕，諸道不甚力，而黃巢方引度江，朝廷度未能制，乃赦之，以國昌為大同軍防禦使。

translations.literal: It was not granted; troops from all circuits were sent to capture them, but the circuits did not exert themselves; Huang Chao was crossing the Yangzi and the court judged it could not control them—so they were pardoned and Guochang made Datong Army defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused. Troops from every circuit were sent to capture them, but the circuits made little effort. Huang Chao was then crossing the Yangzi, and the court judged it could not bring them to heel—so they were pardoned and Guochang was appointed defense commissioner of the Datong Army.

sentences.zh: 國昌不受命，詔河東節度使崔彥昭、幽州張公素共擊之，無功。

translations.literal: Guochang did not accept the order; Military Governors Cui Yanzhao of Hedong and Zhang Gongsu of Youzhou were ordered to attack together, without success.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang refused the appointment. Military Governors Cui Yanzhao of Hedong and Zhang Gongsu of Youzhou were ordered to attack jointly, but achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 國昌與党項戰，未決，大同川吐渾赫連鐸襲振武，盡取其貲械。

translations.literal: Guochang fought the Tangut without decision; on the Datong River the Tuyuhun Helian Duo raided Zhenwu and took all his goods and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang was locked in battle with the Tangut when, on the Datong River, the Tuyuhun Helian Duo raided Zhenwu and carried off all his stores and weapons.

sentences.zh: 國昌窮，挈騎五百還雲州，州不納，鐸遂取之。

translations.literal: Guochang was desperate; he took five hundred horsemen back to Yunzhou; the prefecture would not admit him and Duo took it.
translations.idiomatic: Ruined, Guochang fled with five hundred horsemen to Yunzhou. The city refused him entry, and Duo seized it.

sentences.zh: 克用轉側蔚、朔間，裒兵才三千，屯新城，鐸引萬人圍之，隧而攻，三日不拔，鐸兵殺傷甚。

translations.literal: Keyong shifted between You and Shuo, gathering only three thousand troops; he garrisoned Xincheng; Duo led ten thousand to besiege, attacked by tunnel for three days without taking it, and Duo's army suffered heavy casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong ranged between You and Shuo, mustering barely three thousand men, and garrisoned Xincheng. Duo led ten thousand to besiege him and attacked by tunnel for three days without success; his army suffered heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 國昌自蔚州來，鐸引去。

translations.literal: Guochang came from Youzhou; Duo withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Guochang advanced from Youzhou, Duo withdrew.

sentences.zh: 僖宗以鐸領大同節度，畀討國昌。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong made Duo military governor of Datong and gave him Guochang to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong appointed Duo military governor of Datong and charged him with subduing Guochang.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔昭義李鈞為北面招討使，督潞、太原兵屯代州；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Li Jun of Zhaoyi was made northern campaign commissioner, directing Lu and Taiyuan troops encamped at Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Li Jun of Zhaoyi was appointed northern campaign commissioner, directing Lu and Taiyuan troops encamped at Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 幽州李可舉會鐸攻蔚州，國昌以一隊當之。

translations.literal: Li Keju of Youzhou joined Duo to attack Youzhou; Guochang met them with one detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keju of Youzhou joined Duo in an attack on Youzhou; Guochang met them with a single detachment.

sentences.zh: 克用分兵抵遮虜城拒鈞，天大雪，士仆，鈞眾潰，還代州，軍遂亂，鈞死於兵。

translations.literal: Keyong divided troops to hold Zhelu City against Jun; heaven sent great snow, soldiers fell; Jun's army collapsed, returned to Daizhou, the army then mutinied, and Jun died at the hands of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong detached troops to hold Zhelu City against Li Jun. A blizzard struck, men collapsed in the cold, Jun's army broke and fled back to Daizhou, the force mutinied, and Jun was killed by his own soldiers.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年，以李琢為蔚、朔招討都統，率兵數萬屯代州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangming, Li Zhuo was made overall commander for You and Shuo campaigns, leading tens of thousands encamped at Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangming 1 (880) Li Zhuo was appointed overall commander for the You and Shuo campaigns and led tens of thousands of troops to encamp at Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 克用使傅文達調蔚、朔兵，朔州刺史高文集縛以送琢。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Fu Wenda to muster You and Shuo troops; Shuozhou Prefect Gao Wenji bound him and sent him to Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Fu Wenda to rally the You and Shuo forces, but Shuozhou Prefect Gao Wenji seized him and delivered him to Li Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 琢進攻蔚州，國昌敗，與克用舉宗奔達靼。

translations.literal: Zhuo advanced on Youzhou; Guochang was defeated and fled with Keyong and the whole clan to the Tatars.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhuo advanced on Youzhou. Guochang was defeated and fled with Keyong and the entire clan to the Tatars.

sentences.zh: 鐸密畀酋長圖之，克用得其計，因豪桀大會馳射，百步外針芒木葉無不中，部人大驚，即倡言：「今黃巢北寇，為中原患，一日天子赦我，願與公等南向定天下，庸能終老沙磧哉！」

translations.literal: Duo secretly gave chieftains a plot against them; Keyong learned of it and at a great gathering of heroes held a mounted archery contest—at a hundred paces needle tips and leaves on wood were all hit; the tribesmen were greatly startled, and he proclaimed: "Now Huang Chao raids north and is the scourge of the Central Plains; if the Son of Heaven pardons us one day, I wish to go south with you lords to settle the realm—how can we end our days in the desert sands!
translations.idiomatic: Duo secretly enlisted chieftains to plot against them, but Keyong learned of the scheme. At a grand gathering of tribal leaders he held a mounted archery contest and at a hundred paces struck every needle tip and leaf on wood without fail. His followers were astonished, and he declared: "Huang Chao is raiding northward and ravaging the Central Plains. If the Son of Heaven pardons us, I mean to march south with you and settle the realm—who would spend his life in the desert sands?

sentences.zh: 達靼知不留，乃止。

translations.literal: The Tatars knew they would not be kept and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Tatars, seeing they would not be retained, abandoned the plot.

sentences.zh: 巢攻潼關，入京師，詔河東監軍陳景思發代北軍。

translations.literal: Chao attacked Tong Pass and entered the capital; an edict ordered Hedong Army Supervisor Chen Jingsi to mobilize the Northern Dai army.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao stormed Tong Pass and entered the capital. An edict ordered Hedong Army Supervisor Chen Jingsi to mobilize the Northern Dai forces.

sentences.zh: 時沙陀都督李友金屯興唐軍，薩葛首領米海萬、安慶都督史敬存屯感義軍，克用客塞下，眾數千無所屬。

translations.literal: At that time Shatuo commander Li Youjin garrisoned Xingtang Army; Sige chief Mihaiwan and Anqing commander Shi Jingcun garrisoned Ganyi Army; Keyong sojourned below the frontier pass with several thousand followers belonging to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Shatuo commander Li Youjin was then garrisoned at Xingtang; Sige chief Mihaiwan and Anqing commander Shi Jingcun held Ganyi. Keyong lingered below the frontier pass with several thousand men who answered to no commander.

sentences.zh: 景思聞天子西，乃與友金料騎五千入居絳，兵擅劫帑自私。

translations.literal: Jingsi heard the Son of Heaven had gone west; he and Youjin selected five thousand horsemen and entered Jiang, the troops plundering the treasury for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the emperor had fled west, Jingsi and Youjin mustered five thousand horsemen and entered Jiang, where the troops plundered the treasury for their own gain.

sentences.zh: 還代州，益募士三萬，屯崞西，士囂縱，友金不能制，謀曰：「今合大眾，不得威名宿將，且無功。

translations.literal: Returning to Daizhou, they recruited thirty thousand more and encamped west of Guo; the soldiers were unruly and Youjin could not control them; he plotted, saying, "Now we have gathered a great host—without a renowned veteran general we shall accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Daizhou they raised another thirty thousand men and encamped west of Guo, but the troops grew unruly and Youjin could not control them. "We have assembled a great host," he said, "yet without a renowned veteran commander we will accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 吾兄司徒父子，材而雄，眾所推畏，比得罪於朝，僑戍北部不敢還。

translations.literal: My elder brother the Grand Mentor and his son are talented and bold, feared by all; having lately offended the court, they sojourn in the north and dare not return.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother the Grand Mentor and his son are gifted and formidable, and all men fear them. Having lately offended the court, they linger in the north and dare not return.

sentences.zh: 今若召之使將兵，代北豪英，一呼可集，整行伍，鼓而南，賊不足平也。」

translations.literal: If we summon them to lead the army, the heroes of Northern Dai will gather at a call; array the ranks, beat the drums southward—the rebels are not worth pacifying.
translations.idiomatic: Summon them to lead the army and every hero of Northern Dai will answer at a shout. Put the ranks in order, beat the drums, and march south—the rebels will not stand.

sentences.zh: 景思曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Jingsi said, "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingsi said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 乃丐赦國昌，使討賊贖罪。

translations.literal: They then begged pardon for Guochang and had him attack the rebels to redeem his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: They petitioned for Guochang's pardon and charged him to attack the rebels and redeem his guilt.

sentences.zh: 有詔拜克用代州刺史、忻代兵馬留後，促本軍討賊。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Keyong prefect of Daizhou and acting commander of Xin and Dai horse troops, urging his army to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Keyong prefect of Daizhou and acting commander of the Xin and Dai horse forces, ordering his army to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 克用募達靼萬人，趨代州，將南道太原。

translations.literal: Keyong recruited ten thousand Tatars, hurried to Daizhou, and was about to go south by way of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong recruited ten thousand Tatars, marched to Daizhou, and prepared to advance south through Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 節度使鄭從讜塞石嶺關，不得前，克用儳道至太原，營城下五日，邀糧貲，從讜不答，乃大略，還屯代州。

translations.literal: Military Governor Zheng Congdang blocked Shiling Pass and would not let him pass; Keyong took a bypath to Taiyuan, camped below the city five days, demanded grain and goods; Congdang did not reply, so he plundered greatly and returned to encamp at Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor Zheng Congdang blocked Shiling Pass and refused passage. Keyong slipped by another route to Taiyuan, camped beneath the walls for five days, and demanded supplies. When Congdang refused, he plundered the region and withdrew to Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，蔚州刺史蘇祐會赫連鐸兵將攻代州，克用率騎五百先襲蔚州，下之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe, Youzhou Prefect Su You joined Helian Duo's troops to attack Daizhou; Keyong led five hundred horsemen to strike Youzhou first and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhonghe 2 (882) Youzhou Prefect Su You joined Helian Duo's forces to attack Daizhou. Keyong led five hundred horsemen in a surprise assault on Youzhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 祐屯美女谷，鐸與幽州李可舉眾七萬攻蔚州，譙柵相屬。

translations.literal: You encamped at Meinü Valley; Duo and Li Keju of Youzhou with seventy thousand attacked Youzhou, watchtowers and stockades stretching in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Su You encamped at Meinü Valley while Duo and Li Keju of Youzhou advanced on Youzhou with seventy thousand men, their watchtowers and stockades stretching in an unbroken line.

sentences.zh: 克用直搗營，入蔚州，燔府庫，棄而去，屯雁門。

translations.literal: Keyong drove straight into their camps, entered Youzhou, burned the treasury, abandoned it and left, and encamped at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong drove straight into the enemy camps, entered Youzhou, burned the treasury, abandoned the city, and withdrew to encamp at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 國昌自達靼率兵歸代州。

translations.literal: Guochang led troops back from the Tatars to Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang led his forces back from the Tatars to Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 擾汾、並、樓煩，不釋鎧。

translations.literal: They harassed Fen, Bing, and Loufan, never doffing armor.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Fen, Bing, and Loufan without ever doffing their armor.

sentences.zh: 帝詔克用還軍朔州。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Keyong to return his army to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Keyong to withdraw his army to Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 於是義武節度使王處存、河中節度使王重榮傳詔招克用同討巢。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yiwu Military Governor Wang Chucun and Hezhong Military Governor Wang Zhongrong transmitted the edict inviting Keyong to join in attacking Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu Military Governor Wang Chucun and Hezhong Military Governor Wang Zhongrong then relayed the edict inviting Keyong to join the campaign against Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 克用喜，即大閱雁門，得忻、代、蔚、朔、達靼眾三萬、騎五千而南。

translations.literal: Keyong rejoiced, immediately held a great review at Yanmen, mustered thirty thousand from Xin, Dai, You, Shuo, and the Tatars and five thousand horsemen, and marched south.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong rejoiced, held a grand review at Yanmen, and marched south with thirty thousand men from Xin, Dai, You, Shuo, and the Tatars plus five thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 於是國昌守代州。

translations.literal: Guochang then held Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang remained to hold Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭從讜不肯假道，克用軍傅太原而營，奉幣馬遺從讜，身從數騎呼曰：「我且西，願與公一言。」

translations.literal: Zheng Congdang would not grant passage; Keyong's army camped against Taiyuan, sent gifts of coin and horses to Congdang, and with a few horsemen called out, "I am going west and wish one word with you.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Congdang still refused passage. Keyong's army camped against Taiyuan, sent gifts of coin and horses, and rode forward with only a few followers calling out, "I am marching west and wish a word with you.

sentences.zh: 從讜升陴慰勉，歸貨幣饔餼。

translations.literal: Congdang ascended the wall to encourage him and returned goods, coin, and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Congdang mounted the wall to encourage him and sent down goods, coin, and provisions.

sentences.zh: 克用乃自陰地趨晉，會河中。

translations.literal: Keyong then went from Yindi toward Jin and joined forces at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong then marched from Yindi toward Jin and joined the Hezhong forces.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，擢克用雁門節度、神策天寧軍鎮遏、忻代觀察使。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and promoted Keyong to Yanmen military governor, suppressor of the Shence Tianning Army, and commissioner for Xin and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor promoted Keyong to military governor of Yanmen, suppressor of the Shence Tianning Army, and commissioner for Xin and Dai.

sentences.zh: 明年，宰相王鐸承制，授克用東北面行營都統，河東監軍陳景思為監軍使。

translations.literal: The next year Chancellor Wang Duo, acting by imperial commission, appointed Keyong overall commander of the northeastern campaign army; Hedong Army Supervisor Chen Jingsi was made army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chancellor Wang Duo, acting under imperial commission, appointed Keyong overall commander of the northeastern campaign army, with Hedong Army Supervisor Chen Jingsi as his supervisor.

sentences.zh: 克用使弟克脩領彀騎五百度河，克用自夏陽濟，留薛阿檀扼津口，次同州，壁乾坑，與賊戰梁田坡，敗之。

translations.literal: Keyong sent his younger brother Kexiu with five hundred armored horsemen to cross the river; Keyong himself crossed from Xiayang, left Xue Atan to hold the ford, advanced to Tongzhou, walled at Gankeng, fought the rebels at Liangtian Slope, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent his younger brother Kexiu with five hundred armored horsemen across the river while he himself crossed from Xiayang, left Xue Atan to hold the ford, advanced to Tongzhou, encamped at Gankeng, and routed the rebels at Liangtian Slope.

sentences.zh: 進壁渭橋，遂收京師。

translations.literal: He advanced to wall at Weiqiao and then recovered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Weiqiao and recovered the capital.

sentences.zh: 功第一，進同中書門下平章事、隴西郡公；

translations.literal: His merit ranked first; he was promoted to Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery and Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: His merit ranked first. He was promoted to Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery and enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 國昌為代北軍節度使。

translations.literal: Guochang was made military governor of the Northern Dai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang was appointed military governor of the Northern Dai Army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以克用領河東節度。

translations.literal: Before long Keyong was put in command of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Keyong was given command of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 黃巢與秦宗權合寇河南。

translations.literal: Huang Chao joined with Qin Zongquan to raid Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao allied with Qin Zongquan to ravage Henan.

sentences.zh: 四年，克用率河東、代北兵將自澤、潞下天井關，河陽諸葛爽堙井以拒，克用乃由河中濟，趨許州，合徐、汴兵破尚讓於太康。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Keyong led Hedong and Northern Dai troops intending to descend Tianjing Pass from Ze and Lu; Heyang's Zhuge Shuang blocked the pass; Keyong crossed by Hezhong, hurried to Xuzhou, and with Xu and Bian troops defeated Shang Rang at Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Keyong led Hedong and Northern Dai troops toward Tianjing Pass from Ze and Lu, but Zhuge Shuang of Heyang blocked the pass. Keyong crossed by Hezhong, hurried to Xuzhou, and with Xu and Bian forces defeated Shang Rang at Taikang.

sentences.zh: 戰西華，又破之。

translations.literal: He fought at Xihua and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: At Xihua he defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 賊走，河南平。

translations.literal: The rebels fled and Henan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled and Henan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 追北曹州，還過汴，朱全忠邀之，克用留兵於郊，入舍上源館。

translations.literal: Pursuing north to Caozhou, he returned by way of Bian; Zhu Quanzhong invited him; Keyong left troops in the suburbs and lodged at the Shangyuan Inn.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing north to Caozhou, he returned by way of Bian, where Zhu Quanzhong invited him to stay. Keyong left his troops in the suburbs and took lodging at the Shangyuan Inn.

sentences.zh: 夜帳飲，全忠自佐饔，進貲寶，握手諄勞。

translations.literal: At night they drank in the tent; Quanzhong himself served the feast, presented treasures, and clasped hands in earnest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: That night they feasted in the tent. Quanzhong himself attended the table, presented treasures, and clasped his hands in earnest courtesy.

sentences.zh: 是時，全忠忌克用桀邁難制，則連車外環，陳兵道左右。

translations.literal: At that time Quanzhong resented Keyong's proud spirit as hard to control; he lined wagons in a ring outside and arrayed troops along the roads on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, resenting Keyong's proud spirit as impossible to control, ringed the inn with wagons and posted troops along both roads.

sentences.zh: 克用醉。

translations.literal: Keyong was drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was drunk.

sentences.zh: 乃攻館，下拒戰，親將郭景銖滅燭扶克用，徐告之，尚被酒，乃引弓射。

translations.literal: They then attacked the inn; those below resisted; his personal officer Guo Jingquan extinguished the candles and supported Keyong, telling him slowly; still drunk, he drew his bow and shot.
translations.idiomatic: They then attacked the inn. As fighting broke out below, his personal officer Guo Jingquan snuffed the candles and steadied Keyong, telling him what was happening. Still drunk, Keyong drew his bow and shot.

sentences.zh: 會煙囂四合，大震電，克用與薛誌勤等間關升南譙門，縋走營。

translations.literal: Smoke and dust closed in on all sides; thunder crashed; Keyong with Xue Zhiqin and others made their way up the south gate tower and were lowered by rope to flee to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Smoke and dust closed in on every side as thunder crashed. Keyong, Xue Zhiqin, and a few others fought their way up the south gate tower and were lowered by rope to escape to camp.

sentences.zh: 部下死者數百人，所獲賊乘輿物盡亡之。

translations.literal: Several hundred of his followers died; all the rebel chariots and goods he had taken were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of his followers were killed, and all the rebel chariots and booty he had taken were lost.

sentences.zh: 克用整眾歸太原，益訓兵，將報仇，使弟克勤以萬騎屯河中，乃請擊全忠。

translations.literal: Keyong reorganized his forces and returned to Taiyuan, trained his troops further, planned revenge, sent his younger brother Keqin with ten thousand horsemen to garrison Hezhong, and petitioned to attack Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong reorganized his forces and returned to Taiyuan, redoubled his training, and plotted revenge. He sent his younger brother Keqin with ten thousand horsemen to garrison Hezhong and petitioned to attack Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 使者八返，內外震恐，帝使內謁慰解。

translations.literal: Envoys went back and forth eight times; court and country were terrified; the emperor sent inner attendants to console and mediate.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys shuttled back and forth eight times as court and country trembled. The emperor sent inner attendants to console and mediate.

sentences.zh: 尋進位檢校太傅、隴西郡王。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Acting Grand Tutor and Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Acting Grand Tutor and Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年，幽州李可舉、鎮州王景崇言：「易定故燕、趙境，請取分之。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangqi, Li Keju of Youzhou and Wang Jingchong of Zhenzhou said, "Yiding was formerly Yan and Zhao territory—we ask to take and divide it.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi 1 (885) Li Keju of Youzhou and Wang Jingchong of Zhenzhou petitioned: "Yiding was once Yan and Zhao territory—we ask to seize and partition it.

sentences.zh: 於是可舉攻易州，下之；

translations.literal: Thereupon Keju attacked Yizhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Keju thereupon attacked Yizhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 景崇攻無極。

translations.literal: Jingchong attacked Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong attacked Wuji.

sentences.zh: 易定節度使王處存求救於克用，克用自將救無極，敗鎮人，攻馬頭，固新城。

translations.literal: Yiding Military Governor Wang Chucun begged Keyong for rescue; Keyong personally led troops to save Wuji, defeated the Zhenzhou forces, attacked Matou, and besieged Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yiding Military Governor Wang Chucun begged Keyong for aid. Keyong led the rescue of Wuji in person, routed the Zhenzhou army, attacked Matou, and besieged Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵走，處存復取易州。

translations.literal: The Zhenzhou troops fled; Chucun recovered Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenzhou troops fled and Chucun recovered Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔李昌符、邠寧朱玫與全忠連和，觀軍容使田令孜惡克用與王重榮合，建言：「不可處近輔，請授王處存河中，而徙重榮於易定，則克用孤矣。」

translations.literal: Fengxiang's Li Changfu, Binning's Zhu Mei, and Quanzhong allied; Army Supervisor Tian Lingzi hated Keyong's union with Wang Zhongrong and advised: "He must not remain near the capital—appoint Wang Chucun to Hezhong and move Zhongrong to Yiding, and Keyong will be isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changfu of Fengxiang, Zhu Mei of Binning, and Quanzhong formed an alliance. Army Supervisor Tian Lingzi, resenting Keyong's alliance with Wang Zhongrong, advised: "He must not remain near the capital. Appoint Wang Chucun to Hezhong and transfer Zhongrong to Yiding, and Keyong will stand alone.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 重榮以告，克用怒曰：「我當從公提鼓出汜水關誅全忠，回殲穴鼠耳。」

translations.literal: Zhongrong informed him; Keyong angrily said, "I ought to follow you beating drums out of Sishui Pass to execute Quanzhong, then return to exterminate the burrow rats.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong told him the news. Keyong raged: "I ought to march with you through Sishui Pass and execute Quanzhong, then come back and wipe out the rats in their burrows.

sentences.zh: 重榮計曰：「公兵朝出關，則邠、岐兵夕傅吾堞，願先治邠、岐。」

translations.literal: Zhongrong calculated: "If your army leaves the pass in the morning, Bin and Qi troops will be on our walls by evening—we wish first to deal with Bin and Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong replied: "If your army leaves the pass in the morning, Bin and Qi troops will be on our walls by evening. Deal with Bin and Qi first."

sentences.zh: 克用乃表言：「玫、昌符連全忠為亂，請以兵十五萬度河梟二豎，然後平汴雪大恥，願陛下戒嚴，無為賊所搖。」

translations.literal: Keyong then memorialized: "Mei and Changfu have joined Quanzhong in rebellion—I ask to lead one hundred fifty thousand troops across the river to behead these two wretches, then pacify Bian and wash away the great shame; I pray Your Majesty keep strict guard and not be swayed by the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Keyong memorialized: "Mei and Changfu have joined Quanzhong in rebellion. I ask to lead one hundred fifty thousand troops across the river to behead these two villains, then pacify Bian and avenge this great humiliation. I pray Your Majesty keep strict guard and not be swayed by the rebels."

sentences.zh: 帝遣使慰止，背相望也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to console and restrain him; messengers went back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to console and restrain him, and messages shuttled back and forth.

sentences.zh: 克用不奉詔，玫亦引邠、鳳兵營沙苑。

translations.literal: Keyong did not obey the edict; Mei also led Bin and Feng troops to camp at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong ignored the edict. Mei likewise led Bin and Feng troops to camp at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 克用薄戰，玫敗，夜亡去。

translations.literal: Keyong pressed the attack; Mei was defeated and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong pressed the attack. Mei was defeated and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 克用還河中，天子出趣鳳翔，道傳兵且至，即趣寶雞。

translations.literal: Keyong returned to Hezhong; the Son of Heaven went toward Fengxiang; word spread that troops were coming and he hurried to Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong returned to Hezhong. The emperor set out for Fengxiang, but hearing that troops were approaching, hurried on to Baoji.

sentences.zh: 克用與重榮聯章請還宮，願留兵衛京師，即還鎮。

translations.literal: Keyong and Zhongrong jointly memorialized asking the emperor to return to the palace, offering to leave troops to guard the capital and then return to their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong and Zhongrong jointly petitioned for the emperor's return to the palace, offering to leave troops to guard the capital before returning to their commands.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，走大散關，駐興元。

translations.literal: The emperor was afraid, fled through Dasanguan, and halted at Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the emperor fled through Dasanguan and halted at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 克用引歸。

translations.literal: Keyong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王煴偽詔至太原，克用燔之，執其使，間道奉表興元。

translations.literal: A forged edict of Prince Yun of Xiang reached Taiyuan; Keyong burned it, seized the envoy, and by a secret route sent a memorial to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: A forged edict in the name of Prince Yun of Xiang reached Taiyuan. Keyong burned it, seized the envoy, and sent a memorial to Xingyuan by a secret route.

sentences.zh: 始，朝廷意玫結克用迫乘輿，及表至，示群臣，因騰曉山南諸鎮，行在少安。

translations.literal: At first the court thought Mei had joined Keyong to pressure the imperial carriage; when the memorial arrived it was shown to the ministers, and by proclamation the southern mountain circuits were informed—the traveling court was somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The court had feared Mei and Keyong were jointly pressuring the imperial carriage. When Keyong's memorial arrived it was shown to the ministers and proclaimed to the southern mountain circuits, and the traveling court was somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜斬玫，克用以千騎經略京畿。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu beheaded Mei; Keyong with a thousand horsemen secured the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu beheaded Mei. Keyong secured the capital region with a thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 三年，國昌卒。

translations.literal: In the third year Guochang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Guochang died.

sentences.zh: 俄而昭宗即位，進克用檢校太師兼侍中。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Zhaozong ascended and promoted Keyong to Acting Grand Preceptor and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Emperor Zhaozong ascended the throne, Keyong was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 大順初，克用自攻赫連鐸於雲州，拔東郛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dashun, Keyong himself attacked Helian Duo at Yunzhou and took the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dashun era Keyong personally attacked Helian Duo at Yunzhou and captured the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 幽州李匡威以兵三萬救之，殺其將安金俊，克用走。

translations.literal: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou brought thirty thousand to rescue him, killed his general An Jinjun, and Keyong fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou brought thirty thousand men to the rescue, killed Keyong's general An Jinjun, and Keyong fled.

sentences.zh: 鐸與匡威共建言：「山南亂，克用實首之。

translations.literal: Duo and Kuangwei jointly memorialized: "The turmoil in the southern mountains—Keyong was truly its author.
translations.idiomatic: Duo and Kuangwei jointly memorialized: "The turmoil in the southern mountains was chiefly Keyong's doing.

sentences.zh: 今乘其敗，可伐而取也。」

translations.literal: Now, taking advantage of his defeat, he can be attacked and taken.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is defeated, he can be attacked and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 全忠亦請與河北三鎮共討之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong also asked to join the three Hebei circuits in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong likewise asked to join the three Hebei circuits in attacking him.

sentences.zh: 宰相張浚是其計，乃下制削克用官爵、屬籍，以浚為兵馬招討、制置、宣慰使，京兆尹孫揆副之，樞密使駱全諲為行營都監，華州節度使韓建為行營馬步都虞候兼供軍糧料使，王镕領河東東面，全忠南面，李匡威北面，並為行營招討使。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhang Jun approved the plan; an edict stripped Keyong of office, rank, and clan register; Jun was made campaign commander for horse troops, disposition commissioner, and pacification commissioner; Jingzhao Prefect Sun Kui was his deputy; Privy Councilor Luo Quanqian was campaign supervisor; Huazhou Military Governor Han Jian was campaign horse-and-foot chief adjutant and army provisions commissioner; Wang Rong commanded the eastern Hedong front, Quanzhong the south, Li Kuangwei the north—all as campaign commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhang Jun approved the plan. An edict stripped Keyong of office, rank, and clan register. Zhang Jun was appointed campaign commander, disposition commissioner, and pacification commissioner, with Jingzhao Prefect Sun Kui as deputy, Privy Councilor Luo Quanqian as campaign supervisor, and Huazhou Military Governor Han Jian as chief adjutant and provisions commissioner. Wang Rong commanded the eastern Hedong front, Quanzhong the south, and Li Kuangwei the north—all as campaign commanders.

sentences.zh: 鐸副匡威，先薄戰。

translations.literal: Duo served under Kuangwei and pressed the attack first.
translations.idiomatic: Duo served under Kuangwei and pressed the attack first.

sentences.zh: 克用追潞兵，不肯行，共殺守將李克恭，送款於汴，南首闕下。

translations.literal: Keyong pursued the Lu troops; they refused to march; together they killed the garrison commander Li Kejing, sent submission to Bian, and turned south toward the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong pursued the Lu troops, but they refused to march, killed garrison commander Li Kejing, submitted to Bian, and turned south toward the palace.

sentences.zh: 更詔揆為昭義節度使，克用將李存孝邀揆長子殺之。

translations.literal: Sun Kui was reappointed military governor of Zhaoyi; Keyong's officer Li Cunxiao ambushed and killed Kui's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kui was reappointed military governor of Zhaoyi. Keyong's officer Li Cunxiao ambushed and killed Kui's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 匡威、鐸並吐蕃、黠戛斯眾十萬攻遮虜軍，殺其將劉胡子。

translations.literal: Kuangwei and Duo with Tibetan and Qarluk forces numbering one hundred thousand attacked Zhelu Army and killed its commander Liu Huzi.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei and Duo, with one hundred thousand Tibetan and Qarluk allies, attacked Zhelu Army and killed its commander Liu Huzi.

sentences.zh: 克用乃屯渾河川，存孝與鐸戰樂安，鐸敗走。

translations.literal: Keyong then encamped on the Hun River; Cunxiao fought Duo at Le'an; Duo was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong encamped on the Hun River. Cunxiao fought Duo at Le'an and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 浚入陰地關，壁汾、隰，薛鐵山、李承嗣營洪洞迎戰。

translations.literal: Jun entered Yindi Pass, walled at Fen and Xi; Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi encamped at Hongdong to meet the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun entered Yindi Pass and encamped at Fen and Xi. Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi encamped at Hongdong to meet him.

sentences.zh: 存孝次趙城，韓建夜出壯士三百乘其營，存孝伏以待，建兵大奔。

translations.literal: Cunxiao halted at Zhaocheng; Han Jian sent out three hundred stalwarts by night to strike his camp; Cunxiao lay in ambush; Jian's troops fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao halted at Zhaocheng. Han Jian sent three hundred stalwarts by night to strike his camp, but Cunxiao lay in wait and Jian's men fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 存孝攻絳州，未下，晉州刺史張行恭棄城走，建與浚遁還。

translations.literal: Cunxiao attacked Jiangzhou but did not take it; Jinzhou Prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled; Jian and Jun slipped back.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao attacked Jiangzhou without success. Jinzhou Prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned his city and fled. Han Jian and Zhang Jun withdrew in defeat.

sentences.zh: 明年，克用奉表自陳，乃復拜檢校太師、守中書令、隴西郡王。

translations.literal: The next year Keyong memorialized in his own defense and was again appointed Acting Grand Preceptor, Keeper of the Secretariat, and Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Keyong memorialized in his own defense and was restored as Acting Grand Preceptor, Keeper of the Secretariat, and Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 克用悉兵攻鐸雲州，以騎將薛阿檀為前軍，設伏河上。

translations.literal: Keyong mobilized all troops to attack Duo at Yunzhou, made cavalry commander Xue Atan vanguard, and set an ambush on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong mobilized his entire force against Duo at Yunzhou, made cavalry commander Xue Atan his vanguard, and laid an ambush along the river.

sentences.zh: 鐸縱騎追阿檀，遇伏而奔。

translations.literal: Duo sent horsemen in pursuit of Atan, met the ambush, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Duo sent horsemen in pursuit of Atan, ran into the ambush, and fled.

sentences.zh: 鐸亡入吐渾。

translations.literal: Duo fled into the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Duo fled among the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 克用取雲州，以部將石善友為刺史、大同軍防禦使。

translations.literal: Keyong took Yunzhou and made his officer Shi Shanyou prefect and Datong Army defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong took Yunzhou and appointed his officer Shi Shanyou prefect and defense commissioner of the Datong Army.

sentences.zh: 景福初，鎮州王镕攻堯山，克用使李嗣勛擊之，斬級三萬，克用遂拔天長，略常山，度滹沱，燔其郛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou attacked Yaoshan; Keyong sent Li Sikuen against him and took thirty thousand heads; Keyong then took Tianchang, overran Changshan, crossed the Hutuo, and burned its outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou attacked Yaoshan. Keyong sent Li Sikuen against him and claimed thirty thousand heads. Keyong then took Tianchang, overran Changshan, crossed the Hutuo, and burned its outer walls.

sentences.zh: 徇地至趙，取鼓、槁二城。

translations.literal: He overran the land to Zhao and took the two cities of Gu and Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He overran the country as far as Zhao and took the cities of Gu and Gao.

sentences.zh: 赫連鐸眾八萬攻天成軍，克用飛檄發軍太原，匡威已壁雲州北郊，克用自神堆引軍夜入雲州，死戰，走之。

translations.literal: Helian Duo with eighty thousand attacked Tiancheng Army; Keyong sent urgent orders from Taiyuan; Kuangwei had already walled at the north suburb of Yunzhou; Keyong from Shendui led troops by night into Yunzhou, fought to the death, and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo attacked Tiancheng Army with eighty thousand men. Keyong issued urgent orders from Taiyuan while Kuangwei had already encamped at the north suburb of Yunzhou. Keyong led his men by night from Shendui into Yunzhou, fought savagely, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年，克用次新城，鐸膝行詣軍門降，克用鞭而縱之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianning, Keyong halted at Xincheng; Duo came on his knees to the camp gate to surrender; Keyong whipped him and let him go.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 1 (894) Keyong halted at Xincheng. Duo came on his knees to the camp gate to surrender. Keyong whipped him and let him go.

sentences.zh: 進下武州，攻新州。

translations.literal: He advanced to take Wuzhou and attacked Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Wuzhou and attacked Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 李匡籌引步騎七萬救之，克用迎戰，斬首萬級，俘少將三百，徇城下，新州降。

translations.literal: Li Kuangchou led seventy thousand foot and horse to rescue it; Keyong met him in battle, took ten thousand heads, captured three hundred junior officers, overran below the walls, and Xinzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangchou led seventy thousand foot and horse to the rescue. Keyong met him in battle, claimed ten thousand heads, took three hundred junior officers prisoner, overran the walls, and Xinzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 取媯州，匡籌棄幽州走。

translations.literal: He took Guizhou; Kuangchou abandoned Youzhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He took Guizhou. Kuangchou abandoned Youzhou and fled.

sentences.zh: 明年，幽州降，克用以劉仁恭為留後，乃旋。

translations.literal: The next year Youzhou surrendered; Keyong made Liu Rengong acting commander and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Youzhou surrendered. Keyong appointed Liu Rengong acting commander and returned home.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜、韓建、李茂貞連兵南闕下，殺李溪。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu, Han Jian, and Li Maozhen joined forces south of the palace gates and killed Li Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu, Han Jian, and Li Maozhen joined forces below the southern palace gates and killed Li Xi.

sentences.zh: 克用盡調北部兵度河，拔絳州，斬刺史王瑤。

translations.literal: Keyong mobilized all northern troops across the river, took Jiangzhou, and beheaded Prefect Wang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong mobilized every northern soldier across the river, took Jiangzhou, and beheaded Prefect Wang Yao.

sentences.zh: 次河中，王珂謁於道。

translations.literal: He halted at Hezhong; Wang Ke paid his respects on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Hezhong, where Wang Ke came out to pay his respects along the road.

sentences.zh: 同州王行約奔京師。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyue of Tongzhou fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyue of Tongzhou fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 圍韓建於華州，京師震動，帝為幸石門、莎城，遣內謁郗廷昱慰勞，且言茂貞屯盩厔，行瑜屯興平，克用乃進營渭橋。

translations.literal: He besieged Han Jian at Huazhou; the capital was shaken; the emperor went to Shimen and Shacheng; Inner Attendant Xi Tingyu was sent to console the army and report that Maozhen was at Zhouzhi and Xingyu at Xingping; Keyong then advanced to camp at Weiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Han Jian at Huazhou, throwing the capital into alarm. The emperor withdrew to Shimen and Shacheng and sent Inner Attendant Xi Tingyu to console the army, reporting that Maozhen was encamped at Zhouzhi and Xingyu at Xingping. Keyong then advanced and encamped at Weiqiao.

sentences.zh: 帝以嗣延王戒丕、嗣丹王允詔克用擊邠、鳳。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Prince Jiepi and Prince Dan to command Keyong to attack Bin and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Princes Jiepi and Dan with orders for Keyong to attack Bin and Feng.

sentences.zh: 克用奉詔，屯渭北，遣史儼以票騎三千護石門，且令王珂輸河中粟備行在。

translations.literal: Keyong obeyed the edict, encamped north of the Wei, sent Shi Yan with three thousand swift horsemen to guard Shimen, and ordered Wang Ke to supply Hezhong grain for the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong obeyed the edict, encamped north of the Wei, sent Shi Yan with three thousand swift horsemen to guard Shimen, and ordered Wang Ke to ship Hezhong grain for the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 帝以赤詔嘉答，進克用諸道兵馬都招討使，命二嗣王兄事之，令促討行瑜。

translations.literal: The emperor answered with a vermilion edict of praise, promoted Keyong to overall commander of all circuits' horse troops, ordered the two princes to treat him as an elder brother, and urged swift action against Xingyu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a vermilion edict of praise, promoted Keyong to overall commander of all circuits' forces, instructed the two princes to treat him as an elder brother, and urged him to crush Xingyu quickly.

sentences.zh: 克用請帝還京師，以二千騎衛乘輿。

translations.literal: Keyong asked the emperor to return to Chang'an and provided two thousand horsemen to guard the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong asked the emperor to return to Chang'an and provided two thousand horsemen to guard the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 時宮室煨殘，駐尚書省，百官喪馬，克用進乘輿金具裝二駟，又上百乘給從官。

translations.literal: The palaces were then burned ruins; the court lodged at the Secretariat; officials had lost their horses; Keyong presented two gold-trimmed teams for the imperial carriage and a hundred mounts for attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: The palaces lay in charred ruins and the court lodged at the Secretariat; officials had lost their horses. Keyong presented two gold-trimmed teams for the imperial carriage and a hundred mounts for the attending officials.

sentences.zh: 進太師、兼中書令、邠寧四面行營都統。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Preceptor, concurrently Secretariat Director, and overall commander of the four-sided Binning campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Preceptor, concurrently Secretariat Director, and overall commander of the four-sided Binning campaign army.

sentences.zh: 行瑜堅壁梨園，茂貞自率師三萬逼咸陽而屯。

translations.literal: Xingyu held fast at Liyuan; Maozhen personally led thirty thousand to press Xianyang and encamp.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu held fast at Liyuan while Maozhen personally led thirty thousand men to press Xianyang and encamp nearby.

sentences.zh: 克用請帝責茂貞罷兵，因削官爵，願與河中共討之。

translations.literal: Keyong asked the emperor to rebuke Maozhen and order him to withdraw, strip his rank, and offered to join Hezhong in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong asked the emperor to rebuke Maozhen, order him to withdraw, strip his rank, and offered to join Hezhong in attacking him.

sentences.zh: 帝詔弟事行瑜，貸茂貞，俾結好。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to treat Xingyu as a younger brother, pardon Maozhen, and make peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to treat Xingyu as a younger brother, pardon Maozhen, and seek reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 朱詔賜魏國夫人陳氏。

translations.literal: A vermilion edict ennobled Lady Chen as Duchess of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: A vermilion edict ennobled Lady Chen as Duchess of Wei.

sentences.zh: 陳，襄陽人也，善書，帝所愛，欲急平賊，故予之。

translations.literal: Chen was from Xiangyang, skilled in calligraphy, beloved by the emperor; wishing to pacify the rebels quickly, he granted her this.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was from Xiangyang, skilled in calligraphy, and a favorite of the emperor, who granted her the title in hope of speeding the rebels' defeat.

sentences.zh: 茂貞以兵援龍泉，克用使李罕之、李存審夜引兵劫其餉，援兵亡，行瑜潰而走，追殺萬計。

translations.literal: Maozhen sent troops to aid Longquan; Keyong had Li Hanzhi and Li Cunshen lead troops by night to seize their supplies; the relief force scattered; Xingyu broke and fled; pursuit killed tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen sent troops to relieve Longquan. Keyong had Li Hanzhi and Li Cunshen strike by night and seize their supplies. The relief force scattered, Xingyu's army broke and fled, and the pursuit claimed tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 行瑜入邠州，丐歸款，克用使史儼入其城。

translations.literal: Xingyu entered Binzhou and begged to submit; Keyong sent Shi Yan into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu entered Binzhou and begged to submit. Keyong sent Shi Yan into the city.

sentences.zh: 行瑜死慶州，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Xingyu died at Qingzhou; his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu died at Qingzhou, and his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝悉論幕府官屬及諸子功，封爵之，克用賜號「忠貞平難功臣」，進封晉王。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed the merits of all staff and sons of the headquarters and enfeoffed them; Keyong was granted the title "Loyal and Upright Pacifier of Rebellion" and advanced to Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reviewed the merits of every member of Keyong's staff and household and enfeoffed them accordingly. Keyong was granted the title Loyal and Upright Pacifier of Rebellion and advanced to Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 克用屯雲陽，遣李習吉入朝，且請與王珂悉力討茂貞，帝不許。

translations.literal: Keyong encamped at Yunyang, sent Li Xiji to court, and asked to join Wang Ke in full effort against Maozhen; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong encamped at Yunyang and sent Li Xiji to court, asking to join Wang Ke in an all-out campaign against Maozhen. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 克用私於使者曰：「叛根不除，憂未艾也。」

translations.literal: Keyong told the envoy privately, "If the root of rebellion is not removed, sorrow will not end.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong told the envoy privately, "Until the root of rebellion is cut out, our troubles will not end.

sentences.zh: 天子發度支錢三十萬緡勞其軍。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issued three hundred thousand strings of cash from the treasury to reward his army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued three hundred thousand strings of cash from the treasury to reward his army.

sentences.zh: 時鄆州朱宣兄弟為全忠所困，使來告，克用請道於魏救之。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhu Xuan brothers of Yanzhou were besieged by Quanzhong and sent to plead; Keyong asked passage through Wei to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu Xuan brothers of Yanzhou were then besieged by Quanzhong and sent envoys begging for aid. Keyong asked passage through Wei to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 兵解復鬥，克用自將而往，使李存信率兵三萬與史儼等次於莘，為魏兵所破。

translations.literal: The armies disengaged then fought again; Keyong led in person; he sent Li Cunxin with thirty thousand and Shi Yan and others to halt at Shen; they were defeated by Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: The armies disengaged and then fought again. Keyong led in person while sending Li Cunxin with thirty thousand men and Shi Yan to encamp at Shen, where they were defeated by Wei troops.

sentences.zh: 克用怒，大略相、魏去。

translations.literal: Keyong was enraged and plundered greatly through Xiang and Wei before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was enraged, plundered Xiang and Wei on his way out, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 始，茂貞畏克用見討，修貢獻如藩臣。

translations.literal: At first Maozhen feared Keyong would attack and sent tribute like a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: At first Maozhen feared Keyong would attack him and sent tribute like a vassal lord.

sentences.zh: 及克用還，絕貢獻，與韓建謀以兵入朝。

translations.literal: When Keyong returned, he cut off tribute and plotted with Han Jian to bring troops to court.
translations.idiomatic: Once Keyong withdrew, he cut off tribute and plotted with Han Jian to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，詔克用進衛京師。

translations.literal: The emperor was afraid and ordered Keyong to advance and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the emperor ordered Keyong to advance and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝謀度河幸太原，遣延王入克用軍促迎天子。

translations.literal: The emperor planned to cross the river and go to Taiyuan; he sent Prince Yan into Keyong's army to urge welcoming the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to cross the river to Taiyuan and sent Prince Yan into Keyong's camp to urge him to welcome the throne.
