sentences.zh: 既次渭北，建固請幸華州。

translations.literal: Once halted north of the Wei, Jian firmly asked that the court go to Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court halted north of the Wei, Han Jian pressed hard for a move to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 克用謂王曰：「患本於不斷，顧上自為之。」

translations.literal: Keyong told the prince, "The trouble lies in indecision—the Son of Heaven brings it on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong told the prince, "The trouble lies in indecision—the emperor brings it on himself.

sentences.zh: 李存信攻魏，葛從周引眾三萬來援，戰洹水上，汴人夜坎諸野，哄合，克用子落落馬陷而顛，克用救之，亦顛；

translations.literal: Li Cunxin attacked Wei; Ge Congzhou brought thirty thousand to aid; they fought on the Huan River; Bian troops dug trenches in the fields by night and closed in; Keyong's son Luoluo's horse fell and he was thrown; Keyong rescued him and was thrown as well.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin attacked Wei. Ge Congzhou brought thirty thousand men to the rescue. They fought on the Huan River while Bian troops dug trenches across the fields by night and closed in. Keyong's son Luoluo was thrown when his horse fell; Keyong rushed to save him and was thrown as well.

sentences.zh: 追兵迫，射之乃免。

translations.literal: Pursuers pressed close; he shot and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers pressed close; he shot back and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 存信已傅魏城，克用並力，羅弘信以捉生逆戰，為克用所敗，追及郛，叩闔而還。

translations.literal: Cunxin had already reached Wei city; Keyong joined forces; Luo Hongxin met him with captive-takers in reverse battle and was defeated; pursuit reached the outer wall and they knocked at the gate before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin had already reached Wei city. Keyong joined forces, defeated Luo Hongxin in a sharp counterattack, pursued to the outer wall, and withdrew after pounding on the gates.

sentences.zh: 於是陜州王珙攻河中，李嗣昭援珂，再戰再勝，珙圍解。

translations.literal: Then Wang Gong of Shaanzhou attacked Hezhong; Li Cizhao aided Ke; twice they fought and twice won; Gong's siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong of Shaanzhou then attacked Hezhong. Li Cizhao came to Ke's aid, won twice in succession, and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 帝使延王持節至太原，謂克用曰：「不用卿計，故逮此，無可言者。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Prince Yan with credentials to Taiyuan, saying to Keyong, "Because I did not use your plan, I have come to this—there is nothing more to say.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Prince Yan with credentials to Taiyuan. "Because I did not heed your counsel," he told Keyong, "I have come to this pass. There is nothing more to say.

sentences.zh: 今我寄於華，百司群官無所托，非卿尚誰與憂？

translations.literal: Now I lodge at Hua; the hundred offices and officials have nowhere to rest—if not you, with whom shall I share my cares?
translations.idiomatic: Now I lodge at Hua and the whole bureaucracy has nowhere to stand. If not you, with whom shall I share these cares?

sentences.zh: 不則不復見宗廟矣！」

translations.literal: Otherwise I shall never see the ancestral temples again!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I shall never see the ancestral temples again!

sentences.zh: 王至太原，克用留累月，每大張飲，王必以舞屬克用，因陳國事，涕數行下，冀感動之。

translations.literal: When the prince reached Taiyuan, Keyong kept him many months; at every great feast the prince would offer a dance to Keyong and speak on state affairs with tears streaming, hoping to move him.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince reached Taiyuan, Keyong kept him for many months. At every great feast the prince would dance for Keyong and plead the state's cause with tears streaming down his face, hoping to move him.

sentences.zh: 時劉仁恭據幽州，貳於克用，數召兵不應，克用以書讓之，仁恭得書，抵於地，遂顯絕。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong then held Youzhou, turned disloyal to Keyong, and repeatedly ignored summons for troops; Keyong rebuked him in a letter; Rengong received it, threw it to the ground, and openly broke off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong held Youzhou and had turned against Keyong, repeatedly ignoring summons for troops. Keyong rebuked him in a letter. Rengong threw it to the ground and openly broke with him.

sentences.zh: 故克用內憂幽州，以好辭謝王，不復有西意。

translations.literal: Thus Keyong was inwardly troubled by Youzhou, declined the prince with courteous words, and no longer thought of going west.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was therefore preoccupied with Youzhou, declined the prince with courteous words, and no longer entertained any thought of marching west.

sentences.zh: 俄自將屯蔚州，會晨大雺冥，仁恭來薄戰，克用大敗，走太原，大將多死。

translations.literal: Soon he led in person to encamp at Youzhou; at dawn a great fog fell; Rengong came to press the attack; Keyong was greatly defeated, fled to Taiyuan, and many generals died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he led the army in person to Youzhou. At dawn a thick fog descended. Rengong pressed the attack, Keyong was routed, fled to Taiyuan, and many of his generals fell.

sentences.zh: 全忠奪邢、磁、洺三州，茂貞度克用沮橈，無能出師，乃與韓建謾好，致書言帝暴露累年，請共治宮室迎天子。

translations.literal: Quanzhong seized Xing, Ci, and Ming; Maozhen judged Keyong thwarted and unable to march; he made false peace with Han Jian and wrote that the emperor had been exposed for years, asking to rebuild the palaces together and welcome the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong seized Xing, Ci, and Ming. Maozhen judged Keyong thwarted and unable to march, made a show of peace with Han Jian, and wrote that the emperor had been exposed to the elements for years, proposing that they rebuild the palaces and welcome him back.

sentences.zh: 初，長安自石門之奔，宮殿焚圮，及岐人再逆，火閭里皆盡，宮城昏夜狐貍鳴啼，無人跡。

translations.literal: At first, since the flight through Shimen, Chang'an's palaces were burned and ruined; when the Qi people rebelled again, fires consumed the lanes; at night foxes and badgers cried in the palace city and no human trace remained.
translations.idiomatic: Since the flight through Shimen, Chang'an's palaces had been burned to ruins. When the Qi factions rebelled again, fire consumed the lanes. At night foxes and badgers cried in the palace city where no human footfall remained.

sentences.zh: 帝幸華西溪，望舊京必泫然流涕，左右淒塞不得語。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the western stream at Hua; gazing at the old capital he always wept; those beside him were choked with grief and could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: At the western stream at Hua the emperor gazed toward the old capital and wept every time; those beside him were choked with grief and could not speak.

sentences.zh: 王建方盜兩川，茂貞欲披其鄙私之，數南師，不暇東，而全忠繕治洛陽，茂貞因約克用共其勞，克用辭窮，乃出貲為助。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was seizing the two Sichuan circuits; Maozhen wished to expose his base designs and repeatedly sent southern armies, with no leisure for the east; Quanzhong repaired Luoyang; Maozhen therefore asked Keyong to share the labor; Keyong, pressed hard, contributed funds to help.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was seizing the two Sichuan circuits and Maozhen wished to expose his designs, sending repeated southern campaigns with no leisure for the east. Quanzhong was repairing Luoyang, and Maozhen asked Keyong to share the labor. Hard pressed, Keyong contributed funds.

sentences.zh: 全忠知克用迮不振，乃大舉攻太原，分遣銳將氏叔琮等率魏博、兗鄆、邢洺、義武、晉絳兵環入之，晉城邑多下。

translations.literal: Quanzhong knew Keyong was cramped and not recovering; he launched a great attack on Taiyuan, sending sharp generals like Shi Shuzong with Weibo, Yan-Yun, Xing-Ming, Yiwu, and Jin-Jiang troops to surround and enter; many Jin cities fell.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Keyong was cornered and failing to recover, Quanzhong launched a major assault on Taiyuan. He sent sharp generals such as Shi Shuzong with Weibo, Yan-Yun, Xing-Ming, Yiwu, and Jin-Jiang forces to surround the region, and many Jin cities fell.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，汴兵糧乏，士瘧癘，遂解。

translations.literal: Heavy rain came; Bian troops lacked grain; soldiers fell to malaria; they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains came, Bian supplies ran short, and malaria swept the ranks. The siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 克用雖內憤悒，憚全忠強難與爭，乃厚致幣馬謝，復請修好。

translations.literal: Though inwardly resentful, Keyong feared Quanzhong's strength and difficulty of contest; he sent lavish gifts of coin and horses in apology and again asked for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Though inwardly furious, Keyong feared Quanzhong's strength and sent lavish gifts of coin and horses in apology, again asking for peace.

sentences.zh: 全忠遂取同、華，屯渭上。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then took Tong and Hua and encamped on the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then took Tong and Hua and encamped on the Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝如鳳翔，李茂貞、韓全誨請召克用入衛。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Fengxiang; Li Maozhen and Han Quanhui asked to summon Keyong to guard the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Fengxiang. Li Maozhen and Han Quanhui asked that Keyong be summoned to guard the throne.

sentences.zh: 克用間道遣使者奔問，並詒書全忠勸還汴，全忠不答。

translations.literal: Keyong sent envoys by secret route to inquire hastily and also wrote Quanzhong urging return to Bian; Quanzhong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent envoys by secret routes to inquire after the emperor and wrote Quanzhong urging him to return to Bian. Quanzhong did not reply.

sentences.zh: 克用率兵趨平陽，攻吉上堡，破汴軍於晉州。

translations.literal: Keyong led troops to Pingyang, attacked Jishang Fort, and defeated Bian troops at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong led his army to Pingyang, attacked Jishang Fort, and defeated Bian forces at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭、周德威下慈、隰，進屯河中。

translations.literal: Li Cizhao and Zhou Dewei took Ci and Xi and advanced to encamp at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cizhao and Zhou Dewei took Ci and Xi and advanced to encamp at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 汴將朱友寧以兵十萬壁其南，全忠自屯晉州。

translations.literal: Bian general Zhu Youning with one hundred thousand walled to their south; Quanzhong himself encamped at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bian general Zhu Youning encamped to the south with one hundred thousand men while Quanzhong himself held Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉人聞全忠至，皆失色。

translations.literal: When the Jin people heard Quanzhong had come, all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin armies heard Quanzhong had arrived, every face turned pale.

sentences.zh: 時有虹貫德威營，氏叔琮薄壘疾鬥，晉兵大敗，仗械輜儲皆盡。

translations.literal: A rainbow then spanned Dewei's camp; Shi Shuzong pressed the ramparts in fierce combat; Jin troops were greatly defeated; weapons, gear, and stores were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: A rainbow spanned Dewei's camp. Shi Shuzong pressed the ramparts in fierce fighting. The Jin army was routed and lost all its weapons, gear, and stores.

sentences.zh: 友寧長驅略汾、慈、隰州，皆下，遂圍太原，攻西門。

translations.literal: Youning drove far, overran Fen, Ci, and Xi—all fell—and then besieged Taiyuan, attacking the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: Youning drove deep, overran Fen, Ci, and Xi, and then besieged Taiyuan, assaulting the west gate.

sentences.zh: 德威、嗣昭循山挈餘眾得歸，克用大恐，身荷版築，率士拒守，陰於嗣昭、德威謀奔雲州。

translations.literal: Dewei and Cizhao followed the mountains leading the remnant back; Keyong was greatly afraid, personally carried earthworks, led men in defense, and secretly with Cizhao and Dewei plotted flight to Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei and Cizhao led the survivors back along the mountains. Keyong was terrified, took up a basket himself to work the ramparts, and led the defense while secretly plotting with Cizhao and Dewei to flee to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 李存信曰：「不如依北蕃。」

translations.literal: Li Cunxin said, "Better to rely on the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin said, "Better to submit to the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 國昌妻劉語克用曰：「聞王欲委城入蕃，審乎？

translations.literal: Guochang's wife Lady Liu said to Keyong, "I hear you wish to abandon the city and go among the barbarians—is it so?
translations.idiomatic: Guochang's wife, Lady Liu, said to Keyong, "I hear you mean to abandon the city and flee to the tribes—is it true?

sentences.zh: 計誰出？」

translations.literal: Whose plan is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Whose counsel is this?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「存信等為此。」

translations.literal: He said, "Cunxin and the others propose it."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Cunxin and the others propose it."

sentences.zh: 劉曰：「彼牧羊奴，安辦遠計。

translations.literal: Lady Liu said, "They are sheep-herding slaves—how can they devise far-reaching plans?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu said, "They are sheep-herding slaves—what far-reaching plan can they devise?

sentences.zh: 王常笑王行瑜失城走而死，若何效之？

translations.literal: You often laughed at Wang Xingyu for losing his city, fleeing, and dying—why imitate him?
translations.idiomatic: You often mocked Wang Xingyu for losing his city, fleeing, and dying—why imitate him?

sentences.zh: 且王頃居達靼，危不免。

translations.literal: Moreover, when you lately dwelt among the Tatars, danger was inescapable.
translations.idiomatic: And when you lately lived among the Tatars, danger was inescapable.

sentences.zh: 必一朝去此，禍不旋跬，渠能及北虜哉？」

translations.literal: If you leave here in a morning, disaster will follow at your heels—how can you reach the northern barbarians?"
translations.idiomatic: Leave in the morning and disaster will be on your heels before nightfall—how will you ever reach the northern tribes?"

sentences.zh: 克用悟，乃止。

translations.literal: Keyong understood and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong took her meaning and abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 居數日，散士復集。

translations.literal: After several days scattered soldiers gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: Within days scattered soldiers began to rally again.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭夜擾友寧營，汴人驚，引去。

translations.literal: Cizhao raided Youning's camp by night; the Bian troops were alarmed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cizhao raided Youning's camp by night. The Bian troops panicked and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 德威追之，抵白壁關，復收慈、隰、汾三州。

translations.literal: Dewei pursued to Baiyu Pass and recovered Ci, Xi, and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei pursued them to Baiyu Pass and recovered Ci, Xi, and Fen.

sentences.zh: 三年，克用攻晉州，聞帝自鳳翔還京師，乃去。

translations.literal: In the third year Keyong attacked Jinzhou; hearing the emperor had returned from Fengxiang to the capital, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Keyong attacked Jinzhou, but hearing the emperor had returned from Fengxiang to the capital, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 雲州都將王敬暉殺刺史劉再立，以地予劉仁恭；

translations.literal: Yunzhou commander Wang Jinghui killed Prefect Liu Zaili and gave the territory to Liu Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhou commander Wang Jinghui killed Prefect Liu Zaili and handed the territory to Liu Rengong.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭討之。

translations.literal: Li Cizhao campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cizhao marched against him.

sentences.zh: 仁恭援敬暉，嗣昭壁樂安，欲戰，仁恭取敬暉，棄城去。

translations.literal: Rengong aided Jinghui; Cizhao walled at Le'an and prepared to fight; Rengong took Jinghui and abandoned the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong came to Jinghui's aid. Cizhao encamped at Le'an ready to fight, but Rengong carried Jinghui off and abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 帝東遷，詔至太原，克用泣謂其下曰：「乘輿不復西矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor moved east; when the edict reached Taiyuan, Keyong wept and told his followers, "The imperial carriage will not return west again.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved east and the edict reached Taiyuan, Keyong wept and told his followers, "The imperial carriage will never return west again.

sentences.zh: 遣使者奔問行在，俄加號「協盟同力功臣。」

translations.literal: He sent envoys in haste to inquire after the traveling court; soon he was given the title "Meritorious Ally of Shared Strength."
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys in haste to the traveling court and was soon granted the title Meritorious Ally of Shared Strength.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞、王建與邠州楊崇本遣使者來約義舉，克用顧藩鎮皆附汴，不可與共功，惟契丹阿保機尚可用，乃卑辭召之。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen, Wang Jian, and Yang Chongben of Bin sent envoys to propose a righteous rising; Keyong saw that the military governors all leaned to Bian and could not share the task—only the Khitan Abaoji might still be used; he summoned him with humble words.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen, Wang Jian, and Yang Chongben of Bin sent envoys proposing a joint rising. Keyong saw that the military governors had all thrown in with Bian and could not be relied on—only the Khitan Abaoji might still serve. He summoned him with humble words.

sentences.zh: 保機身到雲中，與克用會，約為兄弟，留十日去，遺馬千匹、牛羊萬計，期冬大舉度河，會昭宗弒而止。

translations.literal: Abaoji came in person to Yunzhong, met Keyong, swore brotherhood, stayed ten days and left, left a thousand horses and tens of thousands of cattle and sheep, and planned a great crossing of the river in winter—stopped when Zhaozong was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji came in person to Yunzhong, met Keyong, and swore brotherhood. After ten days he departed, leaving a thousand horses and vast herds of cattle and sheep. They planned a major river crossing that winter, but the scheme ended when Emperor Zhaozong was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 四年，王建、李茂貞約克用大舉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wang Jian and Li Maozhen urged Keyong to launch a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wang Jian and Li Maozhen urged Keyong to launch a major campaign.

sentences.zh: 建將康晏步騎二萬與克用監軍張承業會鳳翔，是時汴將王重師守長安，劉知俊守同州，與戰長安西，建兵敗，遂不振。

translations.literal: Jian's general Kang Yan with twenty thousand foot and horse joined Keyong's army supervisor Zhang Chengye at Fengxiang; Bian generals Wang Zhongshi held Chang'an and Liu Zhijun held Tongzhou; they fought west of Chang'an; Jian's army was defeated and never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's general Kang Yan brought twenty thousand foot and horse to join Keyong's army supervisor Zhang Chengye at Fengxiang. Bian generals Wang Zhongshi held Chang'an and Liu Zhijun held Tongzhou. They fought west of Chang'an, Jian's army was defeated, and the effort never recovered.

sentences.zh: 唐亡，建與淮南楊渥請克用自王一方，須賊平訪唐宗室立之。

translations.literal: When Tang perished, Jian and Huainan's Yang Wo asked Keyong to declare himself king in one region and, once the rebels were pacified, seek out Tang imperial clansmen to enthrone.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang fell, Jian and Yang Wo of Huainan asked Keyong to declare himself king in one region and, once the rebels were pacified, seek out a member of the Tang imperial house to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 建請悉蜀工制乘輿禦物。

translations.literal: Jian asked that all Sichuan craftsmen make imperial carriage and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Jian asked that all Sichuan craftsmen be set to making imperial carriages and regalia.

sentences.zh: 克用答曰：「自王，非吾誌也。」

translations.literal: Keyong answered, "To make myself king is not my aim.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong answered, "To make myself king is not my aim.

sentences.zh: 建又勸茂貞王岐，茂貞孱褊，亦不敢當，但侈府第、僭宮禁而已。

translations.literal: Jian also urged Maozhen to be king of Qi; Maozhen was weak and narrow-minded and dared not accept, only enlarging his mansion and usurping palace decor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also urged Maozhen to declare himself king of Qi. Maozhen was timid and small-minded and dared not accept, contenting himself with enlarging his mansion and usurping palace decor.

sentences.zh: 建、渥乃自王。

translations.literal: Jian and Wo then declared themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Wo then declared themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 是歲，克用有疾，城門自壞，明年卒。

translations.literal: That year Keyong fell ill; the city gate collapsed of itself; the next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Keyong fell ill and a city gate collapsed on its own. He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：沙陀始歸命天子，仰哺於邊，世喋血助征討，常為邊兵雄。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Shatuo first submitted to the Son of Heaven, fed by the frontier, generation after generation bleeding in aid of campaigns, often the strongest of border troops.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: The Shatuo first submitted to the Son of Heaven and lived on frontier sustenance. Generation after generation they bled in the dynasty's campaigns and were often the strongest troops on the border.

sentences.zh: 至克用逢王室亂，遂有太原。

translations.literal: When Keyong met the royal house in turmoil, he then held Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Keyong came of age amid royal turmoil, he seized Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 虜性惇固，少它腸，自負材果，欲經營天下而不克也。

translations.literal: Barbarian nature is honest and stubborn, with little scheming; trusting his talent and resolve, he wished to manage the realm but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Their nature was blunt and stubborn, with little subtlety. Trusting his talent and resolve, he wished to master the realm but could not.

sentences.zh: 兵雖勝，然數敗；

translations.literal: Though his armies won, they also lost repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: His armies won battles yet lost repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 地雖得，輒復失，故熟視帝劫遷，縮頸羞汗，偷景待僵，不亦鄙乎！

translations.literal: Though he gained territory, he soon lost it again; thus he watched the emperor seized and moved, drew in his neck in shame and sweat, stole time awaiting death—is it not contemptible!
translations.idiomatic: Territory gained was soon lost again. He watched the emperor dragged from capital to capital, shrinking in shame, stealing time while the dynasty stiffened—is that not contemptible?

sentences.zh: 賴其子慓銳，抑而復振。

translations.literal: Only thanks to his son's fierce sharpness was he suppressed yet able to rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Only his son's fierce energy let the house fall and rise again.

sentences.zh: 是時，提兵托勤王者五族，然卒亡朱氏為唐滌恥者，沙陀也。

translations.literal: At that time five clans raised armies claiming to serve the throne, yet in the end it was the Shatuo who destroyed the Zhu house and washed away Tang's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Five houses then raised armies in the name of loyal service, yet in the end it was the Shatuo who destroyed the Zhu and avenged Tang's humiliation.

sentences.zh: 使克用稍知古今，能如齊桓、晉文，唐遽亡乎哉？

translations.literal: Had Keyong known something of past and present and been able like Duke Huan of Qi or Duke Wen of Jin, would Tang have perished so soon?
translations.idiomatic: Had Keyong understood something of history and possessed the stature of Duke Huan of Qi or Duke Wen of Jin, would Tang have fallen so soon?
